title: Propose interactive placeholder collapsing and aria-live updates for autocomplete
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In compact density and long-label scenarios our current text-field placeholder truncates by ellipsis and disappears on focus. For fields with autocomplete or predictive suggestions this causes loss of important context (e.g., units, source, example tokens). Screen-reader users and keyboard-only users also lose the context because aria-labels are inconsistent across implementations.

Goal: Define a single, accessible interaction pattern that preserves contextual tokens and long labels in limited-width inputs across desktop/mobile/compact densities, while staying performant and compatible with server-rendered fallbacks. The solution should be token-aware (respect design tokens for spacing/typography), minimize layout shift, and be implementable with minimal runtime JS for Private customers who restrict bundled scripts.
background:
Recent incident: a customer bug reported confusing billing inputs where unit suffix ("GB/day") was truncated and removed on focus — led to incorrect entries. Accessibility audit flagged that aria-live regions were missing for suggestion list announcements after placeholder collapse. Existing tickets tried incremental fixes (CSS-only truncation, forced tooltips) but introduced flicker and inconsistent keyboard navigation.

Constraints: must work with existing field variants (multiline, password, number), low-motion preference respected, and should degrade gracefully to server-side rendered inputs without JS (static placeholder but visible helper text).
acceptance_criteria: When a long placeholder is present, focusing the field collapses the placeholder into a persistent prefix token (visible and copyable) rather than fully hiding it
Collapsed token is exposed in the accessibility tree and announced via aria-live when the collapse occurs; screen-readers read the full label once on focus
Autocomplete suggestions are announced after token collapse and do not overwrite the prefix announcement; developers can opt into an announcements API
Behavior is consistent across compact and regular density tokens defined in design system (token names referenced below)
CSS-only fallback shows full placeholder below the input as helper text when JS is disabled
Performance: interaction introduces no layout reflow > 8ms on 2x CPU emulation in lab tests
design_decisions: Use a sticky prefix token pattern: the left portion of the placeholder becomes an inline token with reduced opacity and tokenized padding values (token: spacing.input.prefix) on focus
Introduce an ARIA helper: aria-live="polite" region that receives a concatenated string (label + ‘, suggestions available’) to avoid multiple screen-reader interruptions
Expose a lightweight JS opt-in: data-collapse-placeholder="auto" which teams can add to text inputs that require token-aware collapse; default remains off to avoid breaking existing consumers
Motion: animate opacity only (no layout move) and respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling animation and using instant state change
Fallback: server-rendered helper row (class .rs-fallback-helper) renders full placeholder text below the input if JS not available
tradeoffs_and_risks: Adds a small amount of runtime JS for the opt-in behavior—mitigated by keeping it opt-in and small (<4KB gzipped)
Complexity for input types like password / masked inputs; decision is to not collapse for password fields by default to avoid leaking context
Edge cases when combined with prefix/suffix adornments; requires clear priority ordering in CSS and accessibility labeling
Potential for duplicated information if teams already use visible labels—guidance will recommend enabling collapse only when placeholder conveys additional metadata (units/examples)
implementation_notes: Front-end: single small module (collapse-placeholder.js) that toggles collapsed state, updates aria-live node, and toggles .rs--collapsed class
Tokens: use spacing.input.xs for prefix inset, typography.label.small for collapsed token, color.text.muted for opacity
QA: include tests for keyboard-only flow, VoiceOver/NVDA readouts, mobile layout tests at 320px and 360px widths
API: Document data-collapse-placeholder attribute and export a helper (window.RedwoodUI?.collapsePlaceholder) for Private customers to integrate into SSR bootstraps
